Ancestral states

Source: R/predict.R
ancestral.Rd

Posterior distributions of the trait at the internal nodes of the tree (kriging at internal points of the Gaussian process), computed in linear time and averaged over posterior draws. Available for intercept-only models whose kernel is a process along the whole tree: sums of branch-wise components (plus residual or measurement error at the tips), or a single Ornstein-Uhlenbeck component. For Pagel's kappa and delta, reconstructions refer to the transformed tree; for Pagel's lambda, to the tree with internal branches scaled by lambda.

Usage

ancestral(object, ndraws = 500, probs = c(0.05, 0.95), tips = FALSE, seed = 1)

Arguments

object

A phylogp_fit of an intercept-only model (y ~ 1).

ndraws

Number of posterior draws used.

probs

Quantiles to report.

tips

Also return the tips?

seed

Random seed.

Value

A data frame with one row per node (numbered as in object$tree): posterior mean, standard deviation and quantiles.

Details

For OU, reconstructions use the OU process itself, not its branch-wise tip kernel: on an ultrametric tree OU and an accelerating early burst have the same tip distribution but different ancestral states.

References

Schluter D., Price T., Mooers A.Ø., Ludwig D. 1997. Likelihood of ancestor states in adaptive radiation. Evolution. 51:1699–1711.

Garland T. Jr., Ives A.R. 2000. Using the past to predict the present: Confidence intervals for regression equations in phylogenetic comparative methods. The American Naturalist. 155:346–364.
